extractor.prompt: Stage 1 extraction, theme fundierung, per docs/synthesis-operations.md P1.
extractor.note: The 1908 lectures work the founding doctrine on the side of the Kategorialien: the Sachverhalt as the objectuality correlated to the whole assertion, the Sachlage lying at the basis of two states of affairs, non-independent expression-parts with their own non-independent objectual moments, nominalization needing new levels of predication, and categorial ideation founding itself on intuition.

coverage_note: Chapter 2 § 7 and Chapter 4 § 6 in the first run of the text, and §§ 19, 23, 24, 31, 34 b) and 36 b) plus § 8 b) in the second. Not covered: the Introduction, Chapter 1, §§ 5-6 and 8-18, 20-22, 25-30, 32-33, 35, 37-39, and the supplementary texts. Note that Chapters 2-4 appear twice in this file; locators here name the occurrence read.

units.claim: What a categorical proposition says - that the subject-object has such and such a property - is itself an objectuality, the state of affairs.
units.quote: This is an objectuality — precisely this state of affairs (*Sachverhalt*): that that object has such and such a property.

units.claim: Two states of affairs that immediately condition one another have the same situation of affairs at their basis, categorially grasped in different ways.
units.quote: The two states of affairs, immediately conditioning one another, have the same situation of affairs at their basis, which is merely categorially grasped in different ways.

units.claim: The total meaning of an independent expression encompasses the meanings of its non-independent parts, and to every non-independent expression-part there corresponds in a certain way a meant objectual something.
units.quote: The total meaning of an independent expression encompasses the meanings of its non-independent parts; and just as to it as a whole there corresponds a meant objectuality, so too to every non-independent expression-part there corresponds in a certain way a meant objectual something

units.claim: To every meaningful word and word-part there corresponds something objectual, possibly a categorial and non-independent objectual moment.
units.quote: to every meaningful word and word-part there corresponds something objectual — possibly a categorial and non-independent objectual moment

units.claim: Making something objectual where no nominal presentation is present requires new levels of predications with new nominal presentations referred back to and made possible by the lower levels.
units.quote: Every extracting or making-objectual where no nominal presentation is present requires new levels of predications with new nominal presentations referred back to and made possible by the lower levels.

units.term: basic function within the full assertion
units.claim: No thinking is merely nominal presentation: nominal presentation designates a basic function within the full assertion.
units.quote: On the other hand, no thinking is merely nominal presentation. Nominal presentation designates a basic function within the full assertion.

units.claim: The total categorial object, the state of affairs extractable from the judgment, contains as a component the categorial object extractable from the nominal presentation.
units.quote: The total categorial object, the state of affairs extractable from the respective judgment, contains as a component the categorial object extractable from the nominal presentation.

units.claim: Categorial consciousness can build itself upon intuition so that not only the underlying simple acts but the entire consciousness has the character of a giving, perceiving consciousness.
units.quote: categorial consciousness can build itself upon intuition so that not only the underlying simple acts but the entire consciousness has the character of a giving, “perceiving” consciousness

units.claim: A new seeing act founds itself upon the intuition to grasp the essence of the propositionale and every categorial object; this act is categorial ideation or essence-seeing.
units.quote: This means a new gaze — a new seeing act — founds itself upon the one and other intuition, and we call this act ideation (here categorial ideation) or essence-seeing.

units.claim: The covering of categorial apprehensions in the higher layer presupposes the covering of perceptions in the lower layer but goes beyond it.
units.quote: The covering in the higher layer presupposes covering in the lower layer but goes beyond it, since it also involves the identity of categorial forms and conceptual content.

units.claim: Existential states of affairs are given in experience, in perception and the cognition founded on perception.
units.quote: Existential states of affairs are given in experience — in perception and the cognition founded on perception.
